emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(rx_psock)]) from thread_b (the lockless destructor read must not be interleaved by a conflicting concurrent write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: writer serializes the write under mux->rx_lock, but the reader in kcm_rfree reads rx_psock without taking mux->rx_lock; the two accesses share no lock, so no serialize(g) establishes the single-access atomicity the reader assumes
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write to the same pointer -> classic data race (KCSAN reported, value changed under the lockless read)

fix_maps_to: patch adds WRITE_ONCE on reserve/unreserve writes and READ_ONCE on the kcm_rfree read -> makes the single conflicting access atomic, satisfying atomic([read(rx_psock)]); note: this is an annotation, not a lock/ordering guarantee, so it does not map cleanly onto serialize/order/counts
recall_risk_notes: Object and both access sites are in the static surface, so the pair is findable. Risk is on adjudication: the reader is a best-effort re-arm predicate and the writer DOES hold mux->rx_lock, so the LLM may wrongly conclude the field is lock-protected (missing that the reader is lockless) and reject the race, or may judge the torn read benign. The assume is the default implicit-exclusion atomic(single access); no semantic flag-guard exists, so it sits near the 'pure syntactic race' boundary the design warns about.
